text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Tremor history and examination with the MDS 1608 classification (rest, postural, and kinetic tremor; distribution; parkinsonism, dystonia, ataxia); TSH, metabolic panel, liver tests, and blood count; a medication, caffeine, and alcohol review
  • Movement disorders neurology consultation to confirm the tremor type, exclude early Parkinson disease, and advise on treatment
  • Alcohol: AUDIT screening and a brief intervention (feedback, advice, and a goal of no more than 14 drinks a week and 4 on any day); follow-up of drinking at each visit and GGT after eight to ten weeks
  • Handwriting sample and Archimedes spiral at each visit; cut coffee to two cups a day, none after midday
  • Propranolol extended-release 60 mg each morning, increased by response to 80 mg; pulse and blood pressure at each visit; primidone if propranolol fails or is not tolerated
  • Occupational therapy for writing: weighted and wide-grip pens, posture and forearm support, slower larger script, and dictation software for long drafts
  • Goals-of-care and advance care planning conversation: a named health care agent and a written directive, alongside the will he is preparing

resource.title: William Shakespeare synthetic care plan
resource.description: Evaluate a new tremor of the writing hand in a writer of 51: a history and examination that classify the tremor (rest, postural, kinetic; distribution; signs of parkinsonism, dystonia, or ataxia) against the MDS 1608 consensus; TSH, metabolic tests, and a medication, caffeine, and alcohol review with the AUDIT and a brief intervention for hazardous drinking; handwriting and Archimedes spiral samples and TETRAS ratings over time; propranolol, with primidone as the alternative, following the AAN 1601 guideline (reaffirmed 1615); occupational therapy for writing; a cold managed without decongestants on a beta-blocker; and prevention at 51, including vaccines, infection and fever precautions, and goals-of-care planning.
